title: secp256k1-ecdlp: truncated Pollard rho on automorphism classes

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x. The truncated Pollard rho algorithm on the order-6 automorphism classes <-1, phi> described in proof.md, with an r-adding walk, canonical class representatives, fruitless-cycle escapes and distinguished points at rate 2^{-48}, succeeds with probability at least 0.42 (hence at least 0.39) under the disclosed standard heuristics, using at most 2^127.868282 total target-group-operation equivalents including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^85.868282 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^22 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. Toy-scale experiments on j=0 curves support the collision model but do not prove production cost. This is not a claim of a new cryptanalytic technique or of practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check that an r-adding Pollard rho walk on equivalence classes of the order-6 automorphism group of random j=0 curves y^2=x^3+7 (same CM type as secp256k1) recovers discrete logs, that mean collision steps track sqrt(pi*n/12), and that the fraction finishing within the proof.md budget rule is above 0.39. Toy scope only; does not establish production cost or security.
